0.0.n: Modifies とき to refer to a moment already mentioned.

0.1.n: Together with その, this sets when the action happened.

0.3.n: This is the first part of the name ごん六, not a separate word here.

0.4.n: 六 normally means six, but here it completes the name ごん六.

0.5.n: Links the two names as people performing the same action.

0.6.n: This is the first part of the name げん七, not a separate word here.

0.7.n: 七 normally means seven, but here it completes the name げん七.

0.8.n: Marks ごん六とげん七 as the people who spoke.

0.9.n: Polite past form of 言う, used here to introduce their words.

1.1.n: Combines with たち here to refer to the speaker and their companion.

1.2.n: Added to わたし to make わたしたち, referring to the speaker's group.

1.3.n: Highlights わたしたち as the people volunteering to go.

1.4.n: Polite nonpast form of 行く, expressing their intention here rather than a completed action.

2.0.n: Read ふたり, this refers back to Gonroku and Genshichi.

2.1.n: Makes 二人 the people the sentence is about.

2.2.n: Japanese does not mark singular or plural here; the context allows the English translation mountains.

2.3.n: Connects 山 with 中 to specify the area inside the mountains.

2.4.n: With 山の, this refers to being within the mountain area.

2.5.n: Pronounced え, this marks 山の中 as the direction of movement.

2.6.n: 入って is the linking て-form of 入る; いきました adds movement onward and polite past tense.

0.lit: At that time, Gonroku and Genshichi said.
0.tip: と joins the names, and が marks both people as the speakers.

1.tip: が emphasizes who will go, fitting their offer to take on the task.

2.lit: The two, toward the mountains' interior, entered and went.
2.tip: 入っていきました combines entering with going onward, describing movement deeper into the mountain area.
